sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that souls in both lower and higher Gan Eden come to listen to the voices of souls still embodied below, and even those whose service is incomplete can effect a transformation that connects the world to the infinite light of Ein Sof.

translations.translation: And this is the matter of “She who dwells in the gardens,”
the souls that dwell in the lower Gan Eden and in the upper Gan Eden,
come to listen to the voice of the souls of Neshama Elokis below.
For the intention in this is that also the souls,
as they are above prior to their descent into a body,
and also those souls that have already been in a body,
who have the advantage that comes from the service of the body,
for at the time they were in the body, “Days were formed”
“and to Him one of them,”
that they drew down the “one of them” and completed all their service, for which reason they are called “Yisrael, the hosts of Hashem,”
(as explained in the maamar of my father-in-law, the Rebbe, mentioned above),
for “host” has three meanings: first, the term “army,”
that is, acceptance of the yoke.
Second, a fixed time, meaning that in the time fixed for them they complete all their service.
Third, the term “beauty,” meaning beauty,
not only will,
but beauty,
which comes from the innerness of the Keter and causes delight,
and for this reason they are called “the hosts of Hashem.”
Nevertheless, even they come to listen to the voices of the souls that are clothed in bodies,
and even if their service is not yet complete,
neither according to the first meaning of “host”—army, which is acceptance of the yoke,
nor according to the second meaning of “host”—a fixed time, days that are complete and not lacking,
nor according to the third meaning of “host”—beauty,
and as it concludes in the maamar,
that when one studies Torah and does not mention conditions regarding the manner of Torah study,
and performs the mitzvos,
and does not mention conditions regarding the manner of performing mitzvos,
it is transformed from “kesher” (connection) and “sheker” (falsehood),
the falsehood of the world,
into “keresh” (plank),
“planks of shittim wood, standing,”
and they connect the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He, with the world,
a transformation from one extreme to the other,
for one of the permutations of “keresh” is “kesher.”
“Kesher” in holiness means connection.
But in the Other Side, “Do not say ‘kesher’ regarding all that this people says ‘kesher,’”
for their matter is separation and division.
But connection in holiness,
behold, they are all called “chaverim” (companions),
“companions who listen.”
That the souls as they are above,
and also the souls that have already been in a body, who have the advantage of service that comes from the body, for they have completed in this world all their service,
in all three meanings of “host” mentioned above,
all come to listen and receive the voices of the souls clothed in bodies, even though they have not yet completed their service,
for even though they are scattered in exile and graze in the gardens of others,
nevertheless, they tear themselves away from the world and take the body and the animal soul with them, and come to synagogues and study halls, and recite the Shema and engage in Torah,
which is the matter of self-sacrifice from the aspect of Moshiach,
and this is possessed only in this world,
and therefore, “companions,”
also the souls that are in Gan Eden,
listen to their voices,
and also the Holy One, blessed be He, says, “I and My retinue come to hear your voice.”
And this is “Days were formed and to Him,”
and it is not written “and to Him” as a reading,
that through their service—the service of the soul in the body,
with the body and through the body,
they draw down from above the chain of descent into below the chain of descent,
“one of them,”
so that “Hashem is One and His Name is One.”
